value: in a common garden, bud set date ranged from Julian day 217 (White Horse, 60.70 N origin) to Julian day 247 (Fredericton, 46.40 N origin) in 2007
method: outdoor common garden at Indian Head, Saskatchewan (50.33 N, 103.39 W) with natural day length; bud set scored twice weekly on trees from five balsam poplar populations
conditions: Five populations with 15 genotypes each, three replicates per genotype, planted mid-August 2005; the quoted dates are from 2007. Bud flush differed by only a few days among provenances. The paper states high-latitude populations set bud early and rankings were consistent between years in both gardens (data not shown). Day length was not manipulated: the authors read the pattern as photoperiod limiting growth at this site, and their abstract says photoperiod strongly limits height growth in unreplicated outdoor common gardens. The aspen garden at Sävar, Sweden is a separate unreplicated garden and is not logged here.  The paragraph also says height elongation duration and height had strong inverse relationships with latitude in both species (Tables 2, 3, Figure 3).
